title: Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines): To-Value Limit Increase Endorsement
content:
## The endorsement

An increase the named insured signs to raise the excess dwelling limit to the full value the policy allows (a to-value increase) has its additional premium figured under the to-value increase rule; an increase to a stated limit remains under the endorsement rule for limit changes. The additional premium figured for a to-value increase is booked as an endorsement premium item for the current term with the surplus lines tax and stamping fee on it at the policy's recorded rates, in place of re-rating the policy for the full term and pro-rating the change.

## When the additional premium is figured

The additional premium for a limit increase is figured only once the policy record carries the term in which the increase takes effect, from that term's start up to, but not including, its end.

Put the other way round: while the term start and term end on the policy record do not span the day the increase takes effect — that day on or after the term start and before the term end — no additional premium is figured for the increase.

## Capability

`sign_excess_limit_increase_cddf0413` records the named insured's signed request raising the excess dwelling limit of their Excess Flood policy as an endorsement. One call records the signed limit increase with its effective date, the new excess dwelling limit (the excess personal property limit is left as it is) and the full-term premium as endorsed; it updates the policy record to the new excess dwelling limit and the endorsed full-term premium; and it books on the premium account the additional premium given as an endorsement premium item for the current term, together with the surplus lines tax and the stamping fee on it at the rates recorded on the policy (an item that comes to 0.00 is not booked). The amount owed on the policy rises by the items booked, so a credit already standing on the policy is set against them. Success is observable as the endorsement on the servicing record, the new limit on the policy and the endorsement items on the premium account.

## How it is invoked

This is the customer's own tool: the agent unlocks `sign_excess_limit_increase_cddf0413` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it to sign the request.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `excess_policy_id` | the reference number of the insured's Excess Flood policy, as returned by the Excess Flood policy lookup | identifier, as returned |
| `new_excess_building_limit` | the excess dwelling limit after the increase | whole US dollars, integer, no separators |
| `change_effective_date` | the date the increase takes effect | calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD |
| `additional_premium` | the additional premium charged for the increase before taxes | US dollars, 2 decimal places, already rounded to the cent |
| `revised_term_premium` | the full-term premium of the policy as endorsed | US dollars, 2 decimal places, already rounded to the cent |

## Return

On success, a confirmation sentence stating the endorsement reference number, the new excess dwelling limit (whole US dollars), the effective date (YYYY-MM-DD), the additional premium, surplus lines tax and stamping fee booked (USD, 2 decimal places) and the amount owed on the policy afterwards (USD, 2 decimal places; a negative figure is a credit standing in the insured's favour). If no Excess Flood policy has the reference number given, the string says so and nothing is recorded.
